text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition FORD-Kenya party declares its support for the ruling Kenya African National Union party candidate in Tuesday's Langata constituency by-election.
- President Daniel arap Moi urges the Kikuyu and Kalenjin communities to discard tribalism.
- Opposition Democratic Party Chairman Mwai Kibaki rejects calls by some opposition leaders to boycott general election.
- Cattle are dropping dead in drought-ravaged northeastern Kenya, sending livestock prices plunging and bringing financial ruin to fragile economy of Somali herders.
- Mombasa and Zanzibar island plan to become twin towns.
- Mombasa's Women Network Centre will install a telephone hotline for abused women.
- The Roman Catholic church approves women supporting 50 women parliamentary candidates for the general election.
- Raila Odinga, an opposition leader and former member of parliament for Langata, threatens to unleash violence in Langata during Tuesday's by-election.
- Some lawyers in Mombasa are practising illegally with some using forged professional certificates.
- Belgium's recent decision to halt the construction of a Kenyan bullet factory arose from differences with the government over an end-user agreement for munitions from the plant.
- Kenyan oil companies will reduce prices by one shilling if commercial banks lower interest rates from about 25 percent to 15 percent, three points above the rate of inflation.
- Kenya and Tanzania tentatively agree to have common labour legislation. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
